source.title: Learning Curves for Deep Neural Networks: A Gaussian Field Theory Perspective
source.authors: Omry Cohen; Orit Malka; Z. Ringel

record.tranche_reason: The study measures expected and test error for overparameterized neural-network kernel correspondences and reports gradient-trained network results, but it does not test the listed memorization, width, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, sharpness, or example-removal versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports learning curves for regression targets and a hyperparameter experiment on a synthetic hypersphere dataset. It does not report random-label fitting, classification accuracy, or chance-level comparisons. The CIFAR-10 appendix compares kernel predictions and does not report a result on any listed version.
record.test_reason: The study predicts learning curves and compares initialization hyperparameters on synthetic regression tasks. It does not test any listed version: infinite-width generalization alone establishes neither random-label versus natural-label behavior (V1) nor improving test error as width increases past interpolation (V2).
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors report accurate perturbative learning-curve predictions in NTK and NNSP regimes, explain a low-degree polynomial bias for fully connected networks on uniform hypersphere data, and demonstrate improved test loss using theory-guided hyperparameter optimization.
record.recipe_differences: The main learning-curve results use Gaussian-process equivalents of networks in the NTK or NNSP correspondence regimes, rather than the listed studies' interventions. Section VIII also trains a fully connected network with full-batch gradient descent on a synthetic regression task.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported test loss differs across the sampled hyperparameter choices and the optimized choice in Table I.

fits_no_version.finding: On the synthetic hypersphere regression task, optimized initialization hyperparameters give test loss 0.078 versus 0.307 for Typical and 0.175 for the best of 21 random proposals.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Theory-guided initialization hyperparameters can improve test loss for wide fully connected ReLU networks on the tested synthetic regression task.

fits_no_version.finding: The analytical learning curves closely approximate kernel regression results in NTK and NNSP settings; the hypersphere analysis identifies a preference for low-degree polynomial targets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Kernel spectral structure predicts learning curves and a low-degree polynomial bias for fully connected networks in the studied correspondence regimes.

record.problems: The listed versions' interventions and comparisons are not tested. The empirical network experiment uses a synthetic regression target and a single dataset; uncertainty estimates are not stated. The principal learning-curve comparisons in Figure 2 are plotted rather than tabulated.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible rows identified. Figure 2 learning-curve values are shown as plots without tabulated values; the Appendix B CIFAR-10 comparison concerns approximation between kernel predictions, not a listed version.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and training recipe, including chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Test-error changes when width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and compensating training changes.
Dropout effects and their dependence on training-set size, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps and competing measures.
Accuracy after removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All five rows concern an out-of-version hyperparameter comparison. Figure 2 varies dataset size, not network width. Appendix B measures disagreement between kernel predictions on CIFAR-10, not classification generalization or an architecture comparison. Neither supplies a missing test of V1–V8.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out natural-label classification accuracy.
Width sweep across the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected network comparison.
Batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout intervention and its interaction with training-set size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurement and comparison with generalization gaps.
Removal and retraining of memorized examples.
